first.rationale: Current situation presents a direct competitive threat to price-sensitive SMB accounts combined with declining activation and onboarding metrics. Memory 73 demonstrates that targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. Memory 31 shows simplification improved SMB activation durably. However, we face an immediate competitive threat requiring defensive action on the pricing front. Verification of memory_31 and memory_73 will confirm both the magnitude of effect and any retention/quality risks from promotional pricing before scaling. A standard experiment on promotional pricing addresses the immediate competitive pressure while preserves our ability to layer in onboarding simplification or activation messaging in subsequent cycles. This preserves long-term revenue quality by testing defensively now rather than making permanent product changes. The 6% activation decline and 4% onboarding decline may reflect seasonal variance or competitive noise rather than fundamental product issues—promotional pricing pressure requires immediate signal-testing. If promotional pricing shows strong qualified revenue retention, we have defended the segment; if it shows quality risk, we'll have learned that and can pivot to product-focused levers (simplification, messaging) in the next slot.
